correctness.rationale: The reachable plugs starting at the empty boundary are only the empty set, adjacent pairs, and the full set: a full plug forces an empty successor, and an adjacent pair forces either empty or its complement. Thus cutting exactly at empty plugs gives the unique monomer/full-block/alternating-tube decomposition. A square contributes once when it contains opposite matching edges. The internal block counts (1, 4, 2 for a length-two tube, and m-1 for a longer tube) and the common-ring-edge junction count exhaust the three square orientations. The lower bound is the sum of the 2m/3 bounds; equality at length divisible by three singles out length-three tubes and requires A_next != A^c, giving 4 times 3^(k-1). The residue constructions close the rounded bound even at n=1,2. The upper bound uses 3m-2 per block and two per junction; a tube has a strict deficit and a full block at an external junction cannot contribute two. This leaves precisely the uniform layer pairings, plus the isolated full block at n=2. The sixteen reachable layer types count each tiling once and assign each cap and interface exactly once, including the n=1 empty power. Independent direct matching enumeration agrees with both archived full histograms for n=1,...,8. To replay, recursively pair the first unmatched cube with each available neighbor and count flippable unit squares in all three orientations at the leaves; compare the resulting exact histograms with direct_output.txt and transfer_output.txt. The all-n proof is the block and layer argument in RESULT.md lines 25–72, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The established connectivity of the natural face-flip graph does not indicate the available branching at each tiling. The two exact degrees distinguish high- and low-mobility regions and show nontrivial length-three rigidity at the minimum. The transfer formula makes the full local-degree distribution computable for arbitrary lengths without building the reconfiguration graph. These are useful local structural facts for studying flip walks, not claims about distances, mixing, or connectivity novelty.
